requirements.text: Residency in the United States for the last 3 consecutive years
Cross-reference and fact-check claims using regional sources, specialized databases, academic resources, and web directories
Strong fact-checking and critical thinking abilities
Evaluate AI-generated content for factual grounding, hallucination risk, and contextual appropriateness
Deep local cultural awareness and familiarity with regional news, current events, and contemporary culture
Stable broadband internet, a reliable computer, and a smartphone running Android 5.0 or iOS 14 or higher
Active use of Gmail, social media, and web browsers to navigate and interact with varied content
Assess localized content relevancy across news, sports, local culture, and technical topics
Background as a linguist, cross-cultural researcher, or domain specialist with strong research methodology

resumes.text:
Daniel Brooks
Based in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada since 2021

Summary
Fact-checking editor and former local reporter with eight years of experience verifying news for regional and national readers. Careful with sources, clear in written judgments, and attentive to what local communities need to know. I work well independently and take ownership of my assignments from first draft to final correction.

Experience
Senior Fact-Checking Editor, Harbor Ledger Media, remote (2021 to present)
- Review up to 40 articles per week for accuracy. Before publishing, I check each claim against court filings, government databases, and peer-reviewed journals.
- Write structured correction memos explaining each error, its cause, and the fix.
- Trained new checkers on sourcing standards and reviewed their first 100 decisions.
- Built a shared checklist that reduced repeat corrections by about a quarter.

Local Reporter, Cascade Valley Courier, Bend, Oregon (2015 to 2021)
- Covered city council, school board, and community events for six years.
- Assessed which regional stories mattered most to local residents, using readership data and community feedback.
- Published more than 300 stories on housing, transit, and high school sports.

Research Assistant, Northwind Institute, Eugene, Oregon (2013 to 2015)
- Summarized social science studies on public health for policy briefs, applying standard research methods.

Education
B.A. in Journalism, Pacific State University, 2013

Skills
Critical thinking, fact-checking, source verification, AP style, research methods. Gmail for daily work, Facebook, Instagram, and X for community outreach, Chrome and Firefox. iPhone running iOS 17, reliable laptop, fiber broadband at home.

Maya Okafor

Summary
Customer success lead with six years of experience in software support and writing. Professional English fluency, deep local cultural awareness, and a long-time habit of following neighborhood news and community life. I communicate clearly with both customers and volunteers, and I like to work independently on my own projects.

Experience
Customer Success Lead, Brightpath Software (2019 to present)
- Lead a team of nine support agents handling 1,200 tickets weekly.
- Built onboarding guides that cut average resolution time by 30 percent.
- Report monthly service metrics to the leadership group.

Community Blogger, Eastside Neighborhood Journal (2017 to present, part time)
- Write weekly posts on local events, city projects, and neighborhood history.
- Compile background for each piece from county records and regional archives before writing.

Forum Moderator, Hobby Circuit Forums (2015 to 2019)
- Moderated user posts for rule violations such as spam and harassment, using a checklist and removing about 200 flagged entries each month.

Education
B.A. in Communications, Riverside State University, 2015

Skills
Long-form writing, customer support tooling, team leadership, daily work in email, web browsers, and social platforms. Reliable laptop with stable home broadband. Android phone running version 13.

Lucas Ferreira

Summary
Restaurant general manager with nine years of experience running busy dining rooms, staff schedules, and supplier orders. Organized, calm under pressure, and focused on guest satisfaction. Fluent professional English, used every day with staff and suppliers.

Experience
General Manager, Oakline Kitchen and Bar (2017 to present)
- Oversee a team of 35 staff and a budget of 2.4 million dollars per year.
- Reduced food waste by 18 percent through weekly inventory counts and menu changes.
- Hire, train, and schedule servers, cooks, and bartenders.

Assistant Manager, Maple Street Bistro (2014 to 2017)
- Managed nightly service for a 120-seat dining room.
- Resolved guest complaints and coordinated private event bookings.

Floor Server, Harborview Grill (2011 to 2014)
- Served tables during peak shifts and helped onboard new hires on the point-of-sale system.

Education
Associate of Applied Science in Hospitality Management, Lakeshore Community College, 2011

Skills
Inventory control, payroll software, point-of-sale systems, budgeting, staff scheduling. I own a reliable laptop, have stable broadband at home, and use an Android phone running version 13. I use a personal email account and occasionally post on social media. I follow national news and national sports leagues daily, but I do not follow local news closely.
